newborn.definition: A baby from birth to four weeks.
newborn.exampleUsage: The newborn slept peacefully swaddled in a soft cotton blanket.

baby.exampleUsage: The baby smiled when she heard her parent’s familiar voice.

infant.definition: A baby, especially during the first year of life.
infant.exampleUsage: Infant car seats must meet strict pediatric safety regulations.

toddler.definition: A young child who is learning to walk and speak.
toddler.exampleUsage: The curious toddler explored every corner of the playroom.

preschooler.definition: A child who attends a preschool or kindergarten.
preschooler.exampleUsage: The preschooler practiced writing simple numbers with crayons.

child.definition: A young person who has not become an adult.
child.exampleUsage: Every child received a picture storybook during library hour.

kid.definition: An informal word for a child.
kid.exampleUsage: The kids played tag on the open lawn during the afternoon.

youngster.exampleUsage: Local youngsters participated in the neighborhood clean-up day.

childhood.definition: The part of a person's life when they are a child.
childhood.exampleUsage: He fondly remembered his rural childhood spent climbing trees.

growth.definition: The process of becoming larger or developing over time.
growth.exampleUsage: Healthy nutrition supports regular physical and cognitive growth.

teenager.definition: A person aged thirteen to nineteen.
teenager.exampleUsage: The teenager prepared for high school entrance examinations.

adolescent.definition: A young person in the stage between childhood and adulthood.
adolescent.exampleUsage: Adolescent health guidance emphasizes sleep and balanced diet.

teen.definition: An informal word for a teenager.
teen.exampleUsage: Teens gathered at the community center for study sessions.

youth.definition: The period of life between childhood and adulthood.
youth.exampleUsage: The program encouraged youth participation in public service.

puberty.definition: The stage when a young person's body develops toward physical adulthood.
puberty.exampleUsage: Physical changes during puberty mark natural biological growth.

growth-spurt.definition: A brief phase of unusually rapid physical growth during puberty, often marked by increased height and shifting body proportions.
growth-spurt.exampleUsage: A rapid growth spurt meant he needed new shoes within months.

young-adult.definition: A person in the early years of adulthood.
young-adult.exampleUsage: The workshop was designed for young adults starting their careers.

coming-of-age.definition: The process of becoming an adult and taking on adult responsibilities.
coming-of-age.exampleUsage: The graduation ceremony was seen as a coming-of-age milestone.

juvenile.definition: A young person who is not yet an adult, especially in legal contexts.
juvenile.exampleUsage: Juvenile legal protections safeguard underage individuals.

minor.definition: A person who is below the legal age of adulthood.
minor.exampleUsage: A legal minor requires parental consent for travel abroad.

adult.definition: A person who is no longer a child.
adult.exampleUsage: An adult must accompany young visitors inside the museum gallery.

grown-up.definition: An informal word for an adult.
grown-up.exampleUsage: She took on grown-up responsibilities after moving into her own flat.

middle-aged.definition: Describing the stage of adulthood that falls roughly between the ages of forty and sixty-five.
middle-aged.exampleUsage: Middle-aged professionals often seek career renewal programs.

mature.definition: Fully developed in age, ability, or judgment.
mature.exampleUsage: A mature perspective comes from years of practical life experience.

prime.definition: The period when a person or thing is at its best.
prime.exampleUsage: Athletes in their physical prime compete at peak endurance levels.

independent.definition: Free from external control and constraint.
independent.exampleUsage: Living alone taught him how to become fully self-reliant and independent.

responsible.definition: Reliable and able to take care of duties or make sensible decisions.
responsible.exampleUsage: A responsible driver always follows traffic signs and speed limits.

experienced.definition: Having gained knowledge or skill through doing something over time.
experienced.exampleUsage: An experienced teacher guided new instructors through the syllabus.

professional.definition: A person who does work that requires specialized training or skill.
professional.exampleUsage: She maintained a high level of professional conduct in client meetings.

elderly.definition: Relating to people who are old, especially those past middle age.
elderly.exampleUsage: Handrails along the ramp assisted elderly visitors entering the clinic.

senior.definition: An older person, often one who has reached retirement age.
senior.exampleUsage: Senior transit passes offered reduced fares for retired commuters.

retiree.definition: A person who has stopped working, usually after reaching retirement age.
retiree.exampleUsage: As a retiree, he dedicated his weekdays to volunteer gardening.

grandparent.definition: A parent of your father or mother.
grandparent.exampleUsage: Her grandparent shared stories of life in the city decades ago.

aging.exampleUsage: Active walking and reading help maintain health during healthy aging.

wisdom.definition: The ability to make good judgments using knowledge and experience.
wisdom.exampleUsage: Years of leadership gave her the wisdom to resolve disputes calmly.

retirement.definition: The period of life after a person stops working, usually because of age.
retirement.exampleUsage: He planned for a comfortable retirement by saving consistently.

golden-years.definition: An expression for the later years of a person's life.
golden-years.exampleUsage: They spent their golden years traveling to coastal towns together.

elder.definition: A person who is older than you are.
elder.exampleUsage: The community consulted its respected elder on customary matters.

longevity.definition: A long life or the length of time that someone lives.
longevity.exampleUsage: Clean diet and regular exercise contribute to greater longevity.

birth.definition: The event in which a baby is born.
birth.exampleUsage: The certificate recorded the exact date and location of birth.

first-steps.definition: A child's earliest attempts to walk.
first-steps.exampleUsage: The parents celebrated the infant taking his very first steps.

first-words.definition: The first words a young child learns to say.
first-words.exampleUsage: A child’s first words usually include simple familiar names.

school-start.definition: The time when a child first begins attending school.
school-start.exampleUsage: Parents prepared backpacks and uniforms before school start.

graduation.definition: The successful completion of a program of study.
graduation.exampleUsage: Family and friends cheered loudly during the university graduation.

first-job.definition: The first paid job a person has.
first-job.exampleUsage: Her first job at a local bakery taught her time management skills.

marriage.definition: The state of being married or the relationship between spouses.
marriage.exampleUsage: The couple celebrated thirty years of harmonious marriage.

parenthood.definition: The state of being a parent.
parenthood.exampleUsage: Parenthood brought new daily routines and rewarding moments.

legacy.definition: Something a person leaves behind that continues to influence others.
legacy.exampleUsage: The founder left behind an enduring legacy of public service.
